_comment: Every scheduled job on this Mac, with how late it may run before the queue skips it.
maxLateMinutes is the honest question: if this fires now instead of at its cron time,
is the work still worth doing? A nightly sweep landing at 08:30 is noise, so it is
skipped. A Universal Credit check Mica needs is still worth sending at lunchtime, so it
is not. Sweeps get tight limits; anything that touches a person or an obligation gets a
generous one.
mode: 'wrapped' jobs are launchd shell commands run via job-queue.py run, so their PID
proves liveness. 'cooperative' jobs are Claude routines that call acquire and release
from their SKILL.md, where only the lease can free a crashed session.
Crons are standard five-field, LOCAL time, Sunday = 0.
queued:false means the job runs OUTSIDE the queue on purpose. Both such jobs exist to
report on or clean up after the others, so waiting behind a stuck routine would stop them
doing the one thing they are for. They are still listed here so the morning digest watches
needs: what must be true before the job may start. Five of the seven jobs that
failed every day were not broken. They fired the instant the Mac woke, before the
network and Google Drive were up, and reported a hard failure. The queue now waits
up to readyWaitMinutes (default 10) and DEFERS rather than failing if still not
ready. A drive probe READS A BYTE: an unmounted Drive folder still exists and still
lists, and only fails on open with 'Resource deadlock avoided'.
27 Aug 2026: that check runs BEFORE the lock wait, on purpose, so a job waiting for the
network does not hold the queue shut. But the wait is unbounded, and the thing that causes
a long wait here is the Mac sleeping, which is also what kills the network. handback-poll
queued at 08:30 with the network up, waited 43 minutes, took the lock the instant the Mac
woke, and died on DNS. acquire() now RE-PROBES after a wait longer than 60s and DEFERS
instead of failing. The same shape had already hit compound-brain, publish-brain,
masterplan-sync and daily-ops-guard.
8 Aug 2026: the fourteen Claude routines were absorbed into one, `daily-ops`.
Serialising them behind a lock stopped them overwriting each other, then created a
worse failure: a routine suspended by the Mac sleeping keeps HOLDING the lock.
drift-monitor held it 4h54m while asleep, so everything behind it waited and was then
skipped for lateness. A lock cannot fix a machine that sleeps, because the lock sleeps
too. One routine running in sequence has nothing to overlap with and nothing to skip.
The lock now only guards the short shell jobs, and they heartbeat so a sleeping one
frees it in minutes.
them: a job left out of this file entirely is a job nobody notices has stopped.

apple-notes-bridge.queueTimeoutNote: 360 minutes, not the default 120 (finding 20260919-daily-ops-phase2-excepti-548). This job fires straight into content-engine's nightly render, which held the queue for 265, 343 and 253 minutes on 16, 17 and 18 Sep 2026. At 120 it gave up every night without running — twenty queue-timeouts across these five jobs on 15-19 Sep — while needing under fifteen minutes of machine time itself. 360 clears the worst observed hold with headroom. The proper fix is 502's: take the ffmpeg render out of the global lock so content-engine only holds it for its Airtable and Drive writes.

mac-guard.note: reaps preview servers and test browsers that outlived their session. Must run even while a routine holds the queue, since a stuck routine is exactly when strays pile up

job-digest.completedWhenNote: job-digest EXITS 1 BY DESIGN whenever the morning message contains anything needing attention — that is how run-job.sh records a real problem rather than a clean sweep — and it runs outside the queue, so it never writes a `released` event either. Graded on attendance. Found 19 Sep 2026 by the reachability control added with finding 20260919-daily-ops-phase2-excepti-549, which caught it before it produced its own false outage line; daily-ops and data-invariants had to be read on Kevin's screen first.
job-digest.note: reports on the queue, so it must never wait behind it. Wrapped through job-queue.py run + run-job.sh from 14 Sep 2026 (it ran bare before, so the Estate status board could not see it); lock-exempt because it reads the logs and posts a message, never touching the repo or the queue.

daily-ops.completedWhenNote: daily-ops deliberately never takes the queue lock — holding it for two hours would block every short shell job behind it — so it writes `mark` events and never `released`. The default completion test therefore could NEVER go green for it, and the digest of 19 Sep 2026 led with ':no_entry: daily-ops — no completed run in 21 scheduled days' on a job that had run every morning (finding 20260919-daily-ops-phase2-excepti-549). Graded on its own end mark instead.
daily-ops.retryWhenDeferredNote: Deliberately OFF, not forgotten. daily-ops is cooperative and unqueued, so it holds no lock the retry sweep could see: kickstarting it while a session is already mid-run would deliver a second run of a routine that writes code and posts to Slack. daily-ops-guard covers the absence instead, alarming when no phase-1 mark exists by 08:00 London. Revisit only if the guard is retired.
daily-ops.note: THE one Claude routine. Never skipped for lateness (maxLate 1440) — it IS the daily run, and skipping it means nothing happens at all. Unqueued: it runs for an hour or more and must not hold the lock the short shell jobs need.

daily-ops-guard.note: alarms if daily-ops left no phase-1 mark by 08:00 London — the scheduler stamped lastRunAt on 15 Aug 2026 while delivering the run to no session, so only the mark counts. Reports on the routine, so it must never wait behind anything. London gate lives in the code, not this cron (Mac timezone moves with Kevin).

handback-poll.note: Kevin's call, 26 Aug 2026, after measuring the approval loop: the agent's own work on a hand-back is a median of FIVE MINUTES, but he waited a median of 3.6 hours over 1-26 Aug because nothing opened the queue between daily-ops (07:00) and the three triage slots. This checks every half hour and wakes a headless claude run ONLY when a hand-back is actually waiting; a quiet tick is one Airtable read and costs no tokens. HAND-BACKS ONLY (carry_out and redo) — new work, routing and escalation stay in the daily slots. Lateness is deliberately tight: a tick more than 20 minutes late is covered by the next one, so a wake-stampede must not run six of these back to back. The job name is NOT a skill folder name, so check-routines.py sees a registered shell job rather than a second Claude routine. LOCK-EXEMPT from 14 Sep 2026 (Kevin, after the 09:00 inbox triage held the lock for 78 minutes clearing the post-outage backlog while the poll and the board pass queued behind it): the poll touches only Airtable and the approval gate, never the repo or the queue's shared files, and its own gate refuses to start while a dispatch run is in flight (handback-poll.py inflight_run), so it cannot double-carry an action. The cost is a second headless Claude alongside a long slot on a 16 GB Mac; the 45-minute tick ceiling bounds it.
handback-poll.retryWhenDeferredNote: Deliberately OFF, not forgotten. handback-poll runs every 30 minutes, so a deferred slot is picked up by the next one 30 minutes later — re-firing it would add a duplicate poll, not rescue a lost day. Revisit only if the cadence drops below hourly.

roy-assistant.note: Roy's assistant (Kevin, 24 Sep 2026). Roy forwards a message from info@agilelets.co.uk to itself with one line saying what he wants; scripts/roy-assistant.py reads info@'s Sent folder, makes one ROY: task per message for Inbox Response and emails him 'Got it', then this job runs the agent on those tasks straight away, because new work otherwise waits for the 07:00 run or the next triage slot. It also emails Roy what became of each request (the answer, with Kevin, sent, not sent). Every email to a tenant, contractor or agent is still a card in Kevin's one queue. A quiet tick is two Gmail reads and one Airtable read and costs no model tokens: the headless claude run starts only when a Roy request is waiting. Every ten minutes from 07:00 to 20:50; lateness is tight because the next tick is ten minutes away. LOCK-EXEMPT (24 Sep 2026, measured the same day): the inbox triage slots hold the queue lock for a median of 34 minutes (90th percentile 83) three times a day, and the first live tick queued behind the Task Manager slot, so Roy would often wait an hour. Two things make running outside the lock safe: Roy's NEW requests reach a worklist only in the queue read this job makes (ROY_ASSISTANT_RUN=1; every other run lists them under royRequests and leaves them alone), and the runner keeps its own one-tick-at-a-time lock. His approved cards are carried out by the hand-back poll like any other. The job name is not a skill folder, so check-routines.py sees a registered shell job.
roy-assistant.retryWhenDeferredNote: Deliberately OFF: the next tick is ten minutes away, so a re-fire would only add a duplicate run.

retry-deferred.note: Added 27 Aug 2026. launchd fires a job once; if the machine is not ready the queue DEFERS, and until this existed nothing ever came back, so a defer was a lost day and maxLateMinutes allowed lateness nothing could use. The brain went four days unfed that way (24-27 Aug), Drive being unreadable from a sleeping Mac at 22:45 every night. Hourly at :20, OUTSIDE the queue on purpose - it exists to rescue jobs the queue turned away, so waiting behind a stuck routine would stop it doing the one thing it is for. Only re-fires jobs carrying retryWhenDeferred, and REPORTS any other job that deferred rather than silently passing over it.

mcp-inventory.note: Regenerates js/mcp-tools-data.js, the Tools & Connections list on the AI Agents page, from the real MCP configuration (28 Aug 2026). A pure read of local config files plus one `claude mcp list` health check; no AI, no judgement, nothing written outside the repo. Every source has a floor and the run FAILS rather than writing a shorter list, because a list that quietly shrank would read as a smaller estate instead of a broken read. maxLateMinutes is deliberately huge: this Mac sleeps, and the first manual run SKIPPED at 249 minutes late under the original 240. An inventory of what we are connected to is just as true at 4pm as at 6am, so a late refresh beats no refresh. Runs with --publish: when the list genuinely changes it opens a PR carrying the one file, assembled with git plumbing against a throwaway index so it can never disturb another session's uncommitted work in this shared checkout. It never pushes to main. Before publishing it runs the list's own data-shape tests against the candidate and merges only if they pass; a failure leaves the PR open and exits non-zero so the digest catches it.

signature-watch.note: Polls Adobe for documents that have come back signed and files the signed PDF for Kevin's second approval. Four times a day: a signature can land at any hour and the poll costs nothing when nothing is registered, because it exits before opening a browser. Generous lateness on purpose — a signed document is still worth picking up late. NO day-of-week: people sign at weekends.

Scans the raw Drive folder, one episode record per new shooting day, pulls one clip a night to local disk for the render. Drive-gated on the raw folder because a cold stream stalls for 15 min per GB; Lateness capped at 180 min (02:00-05:00) on 4 Sep 2026: at 600 a deferred run could be re-fired by retry-deferred as late as noon, and on 4 Sep that put two renders on the Mac at 11:35 while Kevin was working. content-engine-run.sh also refuses 07:00-21:59 outright, because a manual launch never reads this file. Disk precondition added 9 Sep 2026 (finding 20260909-daily-ops-exceptions-503): 27 GB free against a clip needing ~42 GB of working space, so the render could not finish and held the queue for 4h50m. 60 GB is the working figure from this script's own header (clips 0.3-5 GB, renders and intermediates on top). Below that the run DEFERS with a readable reason instead of taking the lock and stalling everything behind it. maxRuntimeMinutes 540 (11 Sep 2026, finding 20260911-daily-ops-phase-2-522): the 22:00-07:00 window, above the 480 default because three renders take about 7 h.

estate-status.retryWhenDeferredNote: fires every ten minutes, so a missed tick is replaced by the next one; a retry would only double-write the same rows
estate-status.note: Kevin's audit, 14 Sep 2026: 'I have no clue what is published and when, or when agents are not working and when they are.' scripts/estate-status.py mirrors job-status.jsonl, queue-events.jsonl and job-schedule.json into the Estate Status table (one row per live job: last run, worked or not, why in plain words, next due, 24h counts) plus the loop-health not-moving list, and the Estate status tab on the AI Agents page reads it live. LOCK-EXEMPT: it reads the logs and writes Airtable only, never the repo or the queue, so it never waits behind a four-hour render. The page shows 'the status writer itself has stopped' when its rows are older than 30 minutes, so this job cannot fail silently.

utilita-balance.retryWhenDeferredNote: Hourly. A deferred tick is picked up by the next one within the hour, so a retry would only duplicate the read. The daily message is gated by send_decision, not by any single tick.
utilita-balance.note: Hourly on purpose: Utilita's login is a rolling ONE HOUR that every visit restarts, so the read is what holds the session open. utilita-balance.py sends at most one Slack message a day plus one alarm (send_decision), so the other runs are pure keepalive. LOCK-EXEMPT for the same reason as estate-status: it reads a web page and posts to Slack, never the repo, Airtable or the queue, and queueing it behind a four-hour content render would let the session lapse and turn every morning into SIGN-IN NEEDED.

payment-run.note: Kevin's weekly Friday payment run (PRs #483/#484, 18 Sep 2026). launchd com.kevinbrittain.payment-run fires StartCalendarInterval Weekday 5, Hour 21, LOCAL time, and launchd counts Sunday as 0 — so weekday 5 is Friday, which is the same day standard five-field cron means by 5. This entry mirrors that one firing so slot attendance can grade it; it fires nothing itself.
